title: Support-vector regression selects more selective tetrahydropyran catalysts
summary: Models of catalyst fragments and reaction settings selected catalysts for asymmetric tetrahydropyran synthesis. A tested catalyst reached an enantiomeric ratio of 91.5:8.5, above the training examples' maximum of 82:18. The result improves a known catalyst class for a focused reaction; it does not establish invention of the reaction or broad generality.
ai_technology: Support-vector regression with tunable fragment descriptors
organization: Hokkaido University; Max Planck Institute for Coal Research; University of Strasbourg

evidence.tested: Previously untested catalyst substituents were prepared and experimentally evaluated.
evidence.unknown: Exhaustive catalyst prior art, independent replication and broader reaction scope were not assessed.
evidence.ai_role: Support-vector regression with tunable fragment descriptors supported the stated study; experimental and interpretive work remained with researchers.
